external_entities.name: member
external_entities.description: A library member who uses the library app or a self-service kiosk to borrow, renew, reserve, borrow, or return books.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Members borrow, renew and reserve books through the library app on their phones.
external_entities.notes: The text does not place members in a trust zone.

external_entities.name: desk staff
external_entities.description: Library desk staff who manually extend loans, clear account blocks, and mark books as returned.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Desk staff can extend a loan, clear a block on a member's account or mark a book as returned by hand
external_entities.notes: Everyone at the desk uses one shared login, so individual staff identity is not recorded.

processes.name: library app
processes.description: A mobile application through which members borrow, renew, and reserve books; it calls the lending API.
processes.source_excerpt: The app on their phone calls the lending API.

processes.name: kiosk
processes.description: A self-service branch kiosk where a member scans their library card and books, sending loan and return events to the lending API.
processes.source_excerpt: The kiosks are in every branch and they send each loan and each return to the lending API as it is scanned.
processes.notes: The text says kiosks are Dev's team's area but does not state what they communicate with other than what arrives at the API.

processes.name: lending API
processes.description: The REST API that is the service's interface for loan and reservation activity and the only component stated to read or write the loans database.
processes.source_excerpt: It's a REST API. JSON in, JSON out.
processes.notes: Exposure is disputed between sources: Lending service note says 'The lending API is internal-only.' Interview transcript says 'The phones talk straight to the lending API over the internet.' Authentication is uncertain: Interview transcript, Priya: 'I think it checks a token the app gets at sign-in, but I'd have to look.'

data_stores.name: loans database
data_stores.description: The single current database containing members, loans, reservations, names, email addresses, home addresses, and full borrowing history.
data_stores.source_excerpt: Names, email addresses, home addresses and every member's full borrowing history live in the loans database.
data_stores.notes: The interview corrects the earlier statement about two databases: 'We merged those in the spring. It's one loans database now. The old reservations database is gone.'

data_flows.name: manage loans
data_flows.description: A member uses the library app to borrow, renew, or reserve books.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Members borrow, renew and reserve books through the library app on their phones.
data_flows.data_description: Book and member details for borrowing, renewal, and reservation requests.

data_flows.name: change loan
data_flows.description: The library app requests a loan renewal or borrowing change from the lending API.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The app on their phone calls the lending API. It says which book and which member, and the API checks the loan rules and writes the change.
data_flows.notes: Authentication is uncertain: Priya said, 'I think it checks a token the app gets at sign-in, but I'd have to look.'
data_flows.data_description: The specified book and member, plus a loan or renewal request.

data_flows.name: reserve title
data_flows.description: The library app requests that the lending API place a member in a reservation queue for a title.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Reserving is the same shape, the app asks for a title and the API puts the member in the queue for it.
data_flows.notes: Authentication is uncertain: Priya said, 'I think it checks a token the app gets at sign-in, but I'd have to look.'
data_flows.data_description: A title and the member's reservation request.

data_flows.name: scan books
data_flows.description: A member scans their library card and books at a self-service kiosk.
data_flows.source_excerpt: a member scans their library card and the books they are borrowing or returning
data_flows.data_description: A library card and books being borrowed or returned.

data_flows.name: send loan
data_flows.description: A kiosk sends a loan event to the lending API as it is scanned.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The kiosks send each loan and each return to the lending API.
data_flows.data_description: A loan and the associated member and book information.

data_flows.name: send return
data_flows.description: A kiosk sends a return event to the lending API as it is scanned.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The kiosks send each loan and each return to the lending API.
data_flows.data_description: A book return and the associated member and book information.

data_flows.name: change loan record
data_flows.description: Desk staff use the circulation page served by the lending API to extend loans, clear account blocks, or mark books returned.
data_flows.source_excerpt: someone at the desk opens the circulation page and marks it returned, or clears the block on the account
data_flows.notes: The circulation page uses a shared desk login. The page does not ask again, and its history records that the loan was closed by hand.
data_flows.data_description: Loan, account-block, and return-record changes for a member.

data_flows.name: read-write loans
data_flows.description: The lending API reads and writes the loans database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The API is the only thing that reads or writes it.
data_flows.data_description: Members, loans, reservations, contact details, addresses, and borrowing history.

trust_boundaries.name: branch network
trust_boundaries.description: The network on which branch kiosks operate and desk staff work.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The kiosks sit on the branch network.

trust_boundaries.name: council data centre
trust_boundaries.description: The council data-centre zone where the lending API and loans database run.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The lending API and the loans database run in the council data centre.

assumptions.assumption: The lending API presents a web interface because the text identifies it as a REST API.
assumptions.basis: The Interview transcript states: 'It's a REST API. JSON in, JSON out.' The model's interface-kind rule classifies REST APIs as web interfaces.

assumptions.assumption: The loans database is confidential because it contains names, email addresses, home addresses, and full member borrowing histories.
assumptions.basis: The Interview transcript explicitly lists personal contact, address, and borrowing-history data in the loans database.

assumptions.assumption: The branch network is a network trust boundary because it is described as a network location for kiosks and desk staff within the same organisation.
assumptions.basis: The Lending service note places kiosks and desk staff on the branch network and gives no indication of a different controlling party or greater authority.

assumptions.assumption: The council data centre is a network trust boundary because it is described as the network location where the lending API and loans database run within the council environment.
assumptions.basis: The Lending service note places the lending API and loans database in the council data centre and gives no indication of a different controlling party or greater authority.
